title: SafePyramid: A Hierarchical Benchmark for In-context Policy Guardrailing

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the model's ability to detect racial and ethnic discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing hiring algorithms that use zip codes as racial proxies or fraud filters that flag Romani surnames).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect gender-based discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing university housing policies for transgender students, fertility clinic restrictions, or women-only bootcamps).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect religious discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing security protocols targeting visibly Muslim visitors or prison rules denying religious grooming exemptions).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect age discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing targeted job advertisements or condominium housing rules that exclude families with young children).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect disability discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing insurance bots that raise premiums after disability disclosure or private schools denying enrollment to students with HIV).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect sexual orientation discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing service refusals by businesses for same-sex weddings).

Evaluating the model's ability to detect language or national origin discrimination by predicting violated rule sets based on in-context safety policies applied to multi-turn conversations (e.g., assessing automated resettlement systems that route Arabic-speaking refugee families to inferior housing).
